title: [macOS only] Finish the Metal paint-contract port and make gpux green on macOS

checks.descriptionMarkdown: Fails if any source calls the fork-only `adopt_raw_pid(`, or if `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` gain a `[patch` section or a git source. `git grep` exits 1 when nothing matches.

Runs the darwin command module's tests on macOS: the new `command::darwin::process` group and the 27 existing `command::darwin::tests`. The existing tests are selected on purpose, not as a confidence bundle: they have never compiled in gpux, and they are the primary proof that the replacement preserves `darwin.rs` behavior (PROC-3). The red baseline is the current E0599 compile failure on the fork-only API.

CI's own macOS command, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`. A whole-workspace check is justified here: the acceptance criterion is CI parity for `check (macos-latest)`, which runs exactly this command, and per-crate checks cannot prove workspace feature unification or reach every target. It also includes the real `xcrun metal` compile in `gpux-apple`'s build script. No `inputs`, so any product change makes it stale and the final validation re-runs it.
Compiles `gpux-apple` with the `runtime_shaders` feature, which embeds the stitched `scene.h` + `shaders.metal` source.
Compiles `gpux-apple` for iOS. The build script compiles the shaders against the `iphoneos` SDK. Needs `rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios` and Xcode's iOS SDK.
Runs the `paint_packing_*` tests that came with the Metal port; they have never run before.
macOS lint coverage for `gpux-apple`. CI lints only on Windows, where this crate is compiled out.
The new headless Metal pixel test group `metal_paint_contract`, using the precompiled metallib.
The same pixel group compiled with `runtime_shaders`, so Metal compiles the stitched shader source at runtime.
The WGPU dashed-border regression test brought in by the merge of `fix/wgpu-dashed-border-gaps`. It fails when the merge is missing.

Headed Playwright on the Mac: `rayx-dashed-borders.spec.ts` with automatic WebGPU and forced WebGL2, at DPR 1 and 2 (4 tests). RayX must be on `test/dashed-border-gaps` and the sibling `../Gpux` on the integration branch. Not reused, because it depends on a browser, external toolchains and the sibling checkout.
rustfmt check for `gpux-zed-util`. rustfmt formats `cfg(windows)` code too, so this covers the edited Windows test helper even though it cannot compile on macOS.

macOS clippy for the packages whose code this epic changed: `gpux-apple`, `gpux-zed-util` and `gpux-color`. `gpux` and `gpux-wgpu-renderer` changed by one repr line and a test respectively; Windows CI clippy already lints them.
Library tests of the touched packages on macOS. Single-threaded, like CI, because the WGPU tests create GPU devices.

Packaging gate for the manifest change: `gpux-apple` gained a `gpux_color` build-dependency. On macOS this is the only place the packaged `gpux-apple` build script actually runs, so it proves that `GPUX_COLOR_MANIFEST_DIR` finds `src/color/paint.rs` in the packaged `gpux-color` layout.

Existing headed specs that exercise the touched `fs_quad` border, compositing and backend paths, run on the Mac: `rayx-border-antialiasing`, `rayx-srgb-compositing` and `rayx-webgl-fallback` (8 tests across DPR 1 and 2).

sprints.title: Reap macOS child processes without async-process's git fork

tasks.title: Replace adopt_raw_pid with a gpux-owned process handle
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
**Setup (once).**
1. Check out Gpux `fix/metal-paint-contract`.
2. Create the integration branch `macos-only/metal-port-and-ci` from it.
3. Commit `ToFix/` and this epic directory there, unless that was already done when the files were brought to the Mac.
4. Keep RayX on `test/dashed-border-gaps`.
5. Run the red baseline (`check --sprint s1-util-process-reaping --phase baseline`). It must fail on `adopt_raw_pid`.

**Work.**
- Apply the replacement embedded in `ToFix/02-macos-zed-util-process-reaping.md`, or something better that honors d-proc-handle's invariants: the three-line `darwin.rs` diff plus the new `crates/util/src/command/darwin/process.rs`.
- Extend the module's tests into the PROC-2 group. Keep `process_status_waiters_share_one_reaped_status` and `process_kill_ends_a_running_process`, and add:
  - drop-reaps-exited and drop-reaps-later-exit cases;
  - a `kill_on_drop` case;
  - a stress test with at least 50 short-lived children and distinct exit codes, mixing concurrent `status()`, `try_status()` and drops.
- Do not edit or weaken the 27 existing darwin tests.
- Commit, for example as `fix(util): reap posix_spawn children without async-process's git fork`, with a body explaining the crates.io-only rule.

sprints.title: Make CI's macOS check pass for the whole workspace

tasks.title: Fix every remaining macOS-only build error
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` at the Gpux root and fix each macOS-only error in its owning crate, per d-macos-build: no exclusions, no cfg dodges, no git dependencies.

The crates the Windows cross-check could not reach are the likely suspects: `gpux-bench-metrics`, `gpux-http-client-tls`, `gpux-reqwest-client`, and the dev and bench targets of `gpux` and `gpux-platform`.

An error inside `vendor/wgpu` is a blocker to report, not to patch. Commit each fix as its own Conventional Commit; note in the body any fix to an imported upstream file, for d-records. If the check is already green after S1, record that and move on.

tasks.title: Build gpux-apple with runtime_shaders and for iOS
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Check `gpux-apple` with `--features runtime_shaders`, which embeds `stitched_shaders.metal`, and with `--target aarch64-apple-ios`, which takes the build script's `iphoneos` branch and the `-mios-version-min=15.0` Metal flags. Fix what fails in `crates/gpui_apple`.

Prerequisites: `rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios` and Xcode's iOS SDK. If either is missing, install it; do not drop the check.

Prove Metal rendering natively in RayX's Test Suite
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
**Setup.** Keep RayX on `test/dashed-border-gaps`, so `/rendering/dashed-borders` exists, and the sibling `../Gpux` on the integration branch.

**Run.** From `../RayX`, run the Test Suite natively: `cargo run -p xtask -- app apps/test_suite run macos --no-default-features --features rayx_diagnostics,devkit`, with `RAYX_DEVKIT_REGISTRY_DIR` set. Inspect it through `cargo run -p rayx_devkit_mcp -- --connect auto --registry-dir <dir>`, as RayX's `.claude/skills/rayx/references/diagnostics.md` describes.

**Compare.** Walk every PAINT-5 page and hardware double-check, comparing each against headed WebGPU on the same Mac. Store screenshots under `artifacts-temp/agentx/macos-only-metal-port-and-ci-repair/`. Include a crash smoke over every page.

**Repairs.**
- A RayX macOS build error that blocks the run is in scope as a blocker repair in RayX, never in `apps/lab`.
- A rendering defect is fixed in `crates/gpui_apple` and then re-proven by `check-apple-pixels`.

The result decides whether the memory rule on Metal border antialiasing can be closed (DOCS-1).

tasks.title: Merge fix/wgpu-dashed-border-gaps into the integration branch
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Run `git merge fix/wgpu-dashed-border-gaps`, with a merge commit and no rebase. Both branches start at `main` `29702e4` and touch disjoint files, so expect no conflicts; the S6 memory work later builds on `e7149e7`'s WGPU memory edits. Then run the `dashed_border` regression test on macOS.

tasks.title: Run the dashed-border spec on macOS Chromium
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
With RayX on `test/dashed-border-gaps` and `../Gpux` on the integration branch, run `rayx-dashed-borders.spec.ts` through xtask on headed WebGPU. It covers the forced-WebGL2 route at DPR 1 and 2 by itself.

Prerequisites: nightly Rust for `-Z build-std`, `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.129, and `pnpm install` plus Playwright Chromium in `tools-node`. If the setup is partial, recover it with `cargo run -p xtask -- setup-wasm`.

A failure here, with S3 green, points at Chromium-on-macOS differences: investigate before touching the shader.

sprints.title: Harden the flaky upstream Windows process test

tasks.title: Raise spawn_process_tree's pid-file deadline to 30 s
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
In `crates/util/src/process.rs`, change `windows_tests::spawn_process_tree`'s `Duration::from_secs(5)` pid-file deadline to 30 s. Add a one-line comment saying a cold PowerShell start on loaded CI runners can exceed 5 s.

Leave the 50 ms poll, the `powershell -> ping` tree and the 2 s termination check untouched, because they are the behavior under test.

This code is `#[cfg(all(test, windows))]`, so it cannot be compiled here. The focused check is rustfmt; the behavioral proof is CI's `test (windows)` job in S7.

Commit, for example as `test(util): give the grandchild pid file a CI-sized deadline`.

sprints.title: Publish for review with every CI job green

tasks.title: Push, open the paired PRs and get CI green
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Ask the user for explicit approval first. Then:
1. Push `macos-only/metal-port-and-ci`.
2. Open a Gpux PR against `main` with `gh pr create --body-file`. The body covers all four ToFix topics, references the closed rayx-ui/Gpux#1 and #2 as superseded, and lists the exact validation, including what stayed manual.
3. Open or update the RayX PR from `test/dashed-border-gaps` against `master`. Reference the Gpux PR and state that RayX must merge together with it or after it.
4. Wait for all five Gpux CI jobs to go green.

If a job is red, read its log. Fix and push to the same branch: no force-push and no blind re-runs, except for a demonstrated flake.

Do not merge; report the green PRs to the user.
